text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Investors from the United States, Japan, China and Iran have all expressed interest in taking up government's 57 percent shares in joint-venture oil operations.
- Fear grips the wealthy in eastern Nigeria following rumours of impending attacks on associates of a prominent local figure whose hotel was linked to a ritual murder.

- British High Commissioner (ambassador) makes recommendations for the success of government's Vision 2010 proposed economic plan. They include a stable and democratic political atmosphere, privatisation, diversifying the economic base and reduction of debt stock.
- Nigerian Intercontinental Merchant Bank's acquisition of a 70 percent stake in Equity Bank of Nigeria in June has so far cost 400 million naira.

- Exploratory talks have begun between Nigeria and foreign partners in crude oil production on the possibility of converting some of the existing joint venture contracts into production sharing contracts, as a prelude to gradual government disengagement from the sector.

- Proposed trip of finance minister Anthony Ani to the United States has been postponed after visas were not issued to three ministers expected to be on the delegation. The meeting was proposed to discuss Nigerian privatisation with international bankers.
